name: Taurian MPS , Crushing opportunities?
tagline: Small domestic crushing/screening-equipment maker riding India's infra-aggregates capex cycle (revenue Rs11cr->100cr in 3 years), but a HIGH CAUTION governance/cash-flow flag -- statutory auditor resigned Apr-2026, FY26 operating cash flow -Rs37cr, two dilutive capital raises within a year -- caps conviction at Low-Medium despite the genuine growth story.
verdict_headline: Genuine infra-capex tailwind and a real order book (~Rs84cr, Jul-2026), but a statutory-auditor resignation (Apr-2026), deeply negative FY26 operating cash flow (-Rs37cr), and two dilutive capital raises within a year force a HIGH CAUTION red flag that overrides the otherwise-decent four-box score
verdict_reasoning: Statutory auditor BDG & CO LLP resigned effective 14-Apr-2026, ~7 months after the Sep-2025 SME IPO, replaced by Jay Gupta & Associates to fill the casual vacancy -- an explicit HIGH CAUTION trigger per the project's red-flag rules, independent of the growth story

FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs37cr despite Rs16cr reported net profit -- working-capital days ballooned from 108 (FY25) to 227 (FY26) and debtor days to 181, meaning growth is not converting to cash

Two capital raises within a year (Sep-2025 IPO ~Rs42cr + Aug-2026 preferential allotment/warrants ~Rs59cr, further EGM approval Sep-2026) have diluted promoter holding from ~89% pre-IPO to ~63.8% -- a funding treadmill to cover the working-capital gap, not pure growth capex

Four-box score computed at 2.5 (tailwind yes, tam yes, moat weak, valuation no -- 32x trailing P/E on decelerating growth is not cheap) independently lands in the 'neither' band even before the red flag is applied

Growth itself is real and decelerating, not accelerating: revenue YoY +245% (FY24) -> +95% (FY25) -> +35% (FY26); FY27 guidance of 40-50% reacceleration is unconfirmed and rests on a thin, short public disclosure history
Conviction capped at Low-Medium per the HIGH CAUTION rule; thesis_fit forced to neither -- revisit once the auditor transition settles and 2-3 quarters show working-capital normalization
business_overview: Taurian MPS (incorporated 2010, NSE SME-listed Sep-2025) manufactures crushing, screening and washing equipment for mining, construction and waste-recycling/water-treatment applications from a single Roorkee facility (100% in-house manufacturing, current capacity supports ~Rs250cr revenue). Customers include L&T, Jindal Stainless, Tata and Global Atomic; the company sells through 25+ dealers across 20+ countries, recently adding Kenya, Ghana, Thailand and Nepal. ~10% of revenue comes from spares/after-sales. Led by Managing Director Yashvardhan Bajla (24) and his mother as co-promoter.
fundamentals_table: FY25 30% / FY26 ROE 27% (FY26 ROCE not cleanly disclosed)
FY24 Rs11cr, FY25 Rs9cr (declined YoY), FY26 Rs16cr
Rs 25 Cr (low; the real strain is working capital, not term debt)
63.8% (down from ~89% pre-IPO via two raises within a year)
fundamentals_narrative: Taurian MPS is a genuine beneficiary of India's mining/infra-aggregates capex cycle: revenue scaled from Rs11cr (FY23) to ~Rs100cr (FY26), with historically strong ROCE (31-39%) and EBITDA margins around 20-21%. An order book of ~Rs84cr (Jul-2026, 4-5 month execution window) and a growing export dealer network (25+ dealers, 20+ countries, including new Kenya/Ghana/Thailand/Nepal additions) support near-term revenue visibility, and current manufacturing capacity (~Rs250cr) is well ahead of FY26 actual revenue, so no major fresh capex is needed for the next leg of growth. But three things materially temper the story. First, growth is decelerating sharply -- YoY revenue growth went from +245% (FY24) to +95% (FY25) to +35% (FY26) -- even as management guides a 40-50% reacceleration for FY27 off a very short public track record. Second, cash conversion has broken down: FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs37cr despite a reported Rs16cr net profit, as working-capital days nearly doubled (108->227) and debtor days reached 181 -- growth is not yet converting to cash. Third, and most serious, the statutory auditor (BDG & CO LLP) resigned effective 14-Apr-2026, roughly seven months after listing, and was replaced via a casual-vacancy appointment (Jay Gupta & Associates) -- this is an explicit HIGH CAUTION governance trigger independent of the financials. The company has also raised capital twice within a year (the Sep-2025 IPO and an Aug-2026 preferential allotment plus convertible warrants, with a further EGM approval in Sep-2026), diluting promoter holding from ~89% pre-IPO to 63.8% -- consistent with funding a working-capital gap rather than pure growth capex. At 32x trailing P/E on decelerating growth and negative operating cash flow, the stock is not pricing in a margin of safety for any of this.

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Low-Medium. The deep read confirms a genuine infra/mining-capex growth story (revenue Rs11cr->~100cr in 3 years, a real and growing order book) but surfaces a HIGH CAUTION governance flag not visible in the prior light-pass four_box: the statutory auditor resigned 7 months post-IPO (confirmed via direct exchange-filing search), FY26 operating cash flow turned sharply negative (-Rs37cr) on a working-capital blowout, and the company has raised dilutive capital twice within a year. Per the project's red-flag rules, a HIGH CAUTION trigger caps conviction at Low-Medium and forces thesis_fit to neither regardless of the reasonably decent box score (2.5) -- growth and order book momentum are real, but governance/cash-conversion risk dominates the near-term picture.
